concepts.title: Memory Unit Ladder Conversion
concepts.definition: Digital storage sizes climb a fixed ladder where every named step is 1024 of the step below it: kilobyte to megabyte to gigabyte to terabyte and onward up to yottabyte. Turning a big unit into bytes means multiplying by 1024 once per step of the climb.
concepts.key_idea: Each rung of the storage ladder multiplies by 1024, so a gigabyte needs three such rungs to become bytes.
question_patterns: convert 3.7 GB into bytes
how many bytes are there in 1.2 TB of storage
express 2 MB of memory capacity in bytes
a pen drive holds 16 GB; find its capacity in bytes
change 512 KB into bytes showing every step of the conversion
state how many kilobytes make one terabyte

solution_steps.action: climb down one rung from gigabyte to megabyte
solution_steps.explain: 1 GB = 1024 MB, so multiply the gigabyte figure by 1024

solution_steps.action: climb down from megabyte to kilobyte
climb down from kilobyte to byte
solution_steps.explain: 1 KB = 1024 bytes; the third multiplication gives the byte count

worked_examples.q: A phone advertises 128 GB of storage. How many megabytes is that? (1 GB = 1024 MB.)

concepts.title: Bits, Nibble and Byte Sizes
concepts.definition: The atom of computer storage is the bit, holding a single 0 or 1. Four bits grouped side by side form a nibble, and two nibbles (eight bits) form a byte. Counting between these sizes is plain division by 4 and then by 2.
concepts.key_idea: Bits to nibbles is divide by four; nibbles to bytes is divide by two, so a byte always needs eight bits.
concepts.textbook_ref: keip101.txt section 1.3.1, paragraph on bits and words (lines 338-342)
question_patterns: how many nibbles are present in a 32 bit word
define a nibble and state its size in bits
convert 48 bits into bytes
a word is made of 5 nibbles; find how many bits it contains
give two examples of 8 bit binary words that could be bytes
distinguish among a bit, a nibble and a byte by their sizes

solution_steps.explain: one nibble holds 4 bits, so integer-divide the bit count by 4
a byte is two nibbles, so integer-divide the nibble count by 2

worked_examples.q: How many bits make one nibble?

concepts.title: Moore Law Transistor Doubling
concepts.definition: An industry observation credited to Gordon Moore (1965) expected the component count packed onto a single microchip to double roughly every two years, with costs halving at the same pace, which is why chip complexity grew exponentially.
concepts.key_idea: Two years equal one doubling, so divide the elapsed years by two to get the power of two to apply.
concepts.textbook_ref: keip101.txt section 1.2 and Moore's Law note (lines 145-170, 320-328)
question_patterns: state Moore's law in your own words
a microchip carried 2 million transistors in 2000; predict its count in 2010 using Moore's law
according to Moore's law, how many times does the transistor count grow over six years
a processor has 5000 transistors today; estimate the count after eight years assuming doubling every two years
explain why Moore's law describes exponential growth of components on a chip
who proposed Moore's law and in which year

solution_steps.action: count how many two-year doublings fit in the span
solution_steps.explain: the count doubles every 2 years, so integer-divide elapsed years by 2

solution_steps.action: turn the doublings into a growth factor
solution_steps.explain: each doubling multiplies the count by 2, giving 2 raised to the number of doublings

solution_steps.action: scale the starting count by the growth factor
solution_steps.explain: multiply the base transistor count by the factor to project the future count

worked_examples.q: A chip carries 8000 components. After 3 doublings, how many components does it carry?

concepts.title: Primary Memory versus Secondary Memory
concepts.definition: Primary memory (RAM and ROM) is the working store the processor touches directly: RAM holds programs and data only while power stays on, while ROM keeps permanent startup code. Secondary memory such as a hard disk, CD or pen drive is the bigger, slower, non-volatile archive whose contents must first be copied into main memory before the CPU can use them.
concepts.key_idea: RAM is volatile working space, ROM is read-only permanent code, and secondary storage is the large non-volatile archive.
question_patterns: why is RAM called a volatile memory
differentiate between RAM and ROM, giving one use of each
state the need for secondary memory in a computer system
which type of memory stores the boot loader that loads the operating system
why must data on a hard disk be brought into main memory before processing
name any two secondary storage devices found in a school computer lab

solution_steps.action: check the behaviour of each memory on power loss
solution_steps.explain: RAM empties when power goes off; ROM and secondary storage keep their contents

solution_steps.action: check who can reach the store directly
solution_steps.explain: the CPU addresses primary memory directly, but secondary storage must be staged through main memory

solution_steps.action: match the purpose to the memory type
solution_steps.explain: temporary working data goes to RAM, rarely changed startup code to ROM, permanent bulk data to secondary memory

worked_examples.q: Which primary memory keeps permanent startup code?

concepts.title: CPU Parts: ALU, Control Unit and Registers
concepts.definition: Inside the processor, the arithmetic logic unit carries out every calculation and comparison, the control unit sequences the instructions and steers data between memory, ALU and input/output devices, and small on-chip registers hold the data and intermediate results currently in use.
concepts.key_idea: ALU computes, CU directs, registers hold what is being worked on this instant.
question_patterns: name the two main components of the CPU and state the role of each
what job does the control unit perform in a processor
where does the CPU keep data and instructions while processing them
why is the CPU often described as the brain of the computer
list two arithmetic and two logic operations that the ALU performs
state what registers are and why they are limited in size and number

solution_steps.action: separate the computing part from the directing part
solution_steps.explain: the ALU does arithmetic and logic; the CU interprets instructions and guides data flow

solution_steps.action: locate the temporary storage inside the chip
solution_steps.explain: registers sit on the CPU itself and store data, instructions and intermediate results

solution_steps.action: trace one instruction through the parts
solution_steps.explain: the CU fetches the instruction, the ALU computes on register values, results return to memory

worked_examples.q: Which CPU part carries out every calculation and comparison?

concepts.title: Software Categories and FOSS Licensing
concepts.definition: Programs fall into three broad families: system software that runs the machine (operating systems, utilities, device drivers), programming tools that build new software, and application software that serves end users, split into general purpose and customised kinds. By availability, software may be FOSS with open source code, freeware free to use but closed, or proprietary software bought from its copyright owner.
concepts.key_idea: A computer can run without application software but never without system software, and open source means the code itself is public.
question_patterns: differentiate between proprietary software and freeware, naming two programs of each kind
identify the category (system, application, programming tool) of a compiler, an assembler, Ubuntu and a text editor
what is free and open source software? give two examples
why can a computer work without application software but not without an operating system
state the role of a device driver in a computer system
name the software that acts as an interface between the user and the hardware

solution_steps.explain: system software serves the machine and other programs; application software serves the end user

solution_steps.action: check whether source code is published
solution_steps.explain: FOSS publishes its source code for anyone to improve; freeware and proprietary software keep it closed

solution_steps.action: check how usage is paid for
solution_steps.explain: proprietary software must be purchased from the vendor; freeware costs nothing to use; FOSS is free with open code

worked_examples.q: Which software family can a computer never run without: system or application software?
